set.st: March 1934: CCC worker Stanley Wojtysiak, razing the 100-year-old Kammeyer grist mill at Fullersburg, chopped into a brick wall and a tin box of old $10 and $20 bills (about $4,200) fell out. When the former operator Kammeyer died, relatives from Rome, N.Y. had searched in vain for his $4,000+ savings. Recovered March 1934; the mill was razed; nothing more reported. The Tribune's location is the Graue Mill site at York and Spring roads, where the CCC was rebuilding the dam in 1934, so the 'Kammeyer mill' of the wire story is most likely Graue Mill itself under a later operator's name, or an outbuilding of it; the 1934 reports call it a 100-year-old mill being torn down, which fits the CCC demolition of the old wheelhouse and dam rather than the main building. The Tribune names the finder Stanley Wojtysiak and places the mill at York and Spring roads; he disputed the $4,200 total.
set.pl: Graue Mill site, Salt Creek at York and Spring roads, Fullersburg (forest preserve, look only); pin is GNIS Fullersburg, within about 0.8 km
set.t: Found. Fullersburg Woods is a forest preserve: no detecting. Access: forest preserve: look only. The mill is a museum; nothing to search.

Chicago Tribune 1934 places the mill on Salt Creek at York and Spring roads, the Graue Mill site. No mapped point for the mill could be checked from here (Wikipedia gives only 41.82, -87.928), so the pin stays on GNIS Fullersburg with r800 covering the site.
